messages.author: a3527f6489543e9b
messages.subject: Clipping issues with AX3 data
parts:
Dear GGIR community

I currently use GGIR (v 2.9-0) to analyse 24-hour data collected over 9 days using Axivity AX3. I noticed that the clipping scores in the part2summary were unusually high for most of the data files that I have analysed so far (23/36 with a score >0.1):

I am also getting these warning messages from the analysis:


I have not had these issues before with the previous analyses of AX3 data files. I also tried using the previous version of GGIR (2.8-2), which gave me the same output type. 
I have gone through the conversations within the group and found a post from Ruth Salway (September 9, 2022), who had a similar clipping issue with the AX6 Axivity data. Has anyone else encountered this issue using the most recent version of the package? I have attached my config. csv file in this email as well. 

Thank you.

Best regards,
John.

Best,

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Clipping issues with AX3 data
parts:
Thanks John for reporting this and thanks Jairo for having a first look.

I have looked into it and it looks like this is a bug introduced in the GGIRread release 0.2.7 from last week.

I have now prepared a fix, to test this please update GGIRread with:

remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIRread", ref = "issue29_axivity_variable_sf")

Sorry about this, I did not foresee that this could be a bug and I may have been a bit too excited about the speed increase. The speed increase should not be affected

Best,

Vincent

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Clipping issues with AX3 data
parts:
Hi John

I have made some updates now and tested them on the two files you shared and it looks much better now. In the GGIR QC plot I see a little bit of clipping in the beginning of the recording, but generally it looks better now. When I inspect the file with OMGUI I see a genuine 5 hour time jump at the beginning and also when i was working with your data I noticed significant drops in sample rate relate to the specified sampling rate. So, I think there is something wrong with these files and I think it is best if you could contact the manufacture.

Happy to investigate more, but that would then have to be part of a paid consultancy (GGIR is free software but my time is not).

Best,

Vincent
